title: Eales Disease: The Enigmatic Peripheral Perivasculitis
summary: A primary idiopathic inflammatory venous occlusive disease of the peripheral retina, predominantly affecting young healthy males. It is characterized by three distinct stages: perivascular inflammation, peripheral ischemia, and retinal neovascularization.

sections.title: 1. Definition & Clinical Overview
sections.content: Eales disease is an idiopathic, inflammatory, peripheral retinal venulitis characterized by stages of inflammation (sheathing), non-perfusion (ischemia), and neovascularization. It is a diagnosis of exclusion and primarily affects the peripheral retina, often leading to recurrent vitreous hemorrhages.

branches: High prevalence of HLA-B5, DR1, DR4

rows: Neovascularization elsewhere (NVE) or on the Disc (NVD)
Complications: Rubeosis Iridis, NVG, Phthisis Bulbi

sections.title: 5. Ocular Examination Findings
content: Vascular Sheathing: Peripheral venous 'cuffing' (exudative white lines).
Venous Tortuosity: Dilated, beaded peripheral veins.
Peripheral Hemorrhages: Flame-shaped or dot-blot in the periphery.
Neovascularization: Classic 'Sea-fan' pattern at the junction of perfused/non-perfused retina.
Macular Edema: Cystoid changes due to chronic inflammation.
Vitreous: Cells (1+ to 3+), haze, or frank hemorrhage.

rows: Massive exudation; Telangiectatic vessels; usually unilateral
Sectoral; follows anatomy of vein crossing

sections.title: 7. Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: Step 1: Ultra-Widefield FFA — Identify peripheral capillary non-perfusion (CNP) and NVE.
Step 2: Mantoux Test / QuantiFERON-TB Gold — Screen for TB hypersensitivity/exposure.
Step 3: Chest X-Ray — Rule out active TB or Sarcoidosis.
Step 4: Blood Panel — CBC, ESR, ESR, ANA, ACE, VDRL/RPR to exclude other vasculitides.
Step 5: B-Scan Ultrasonography — Essential when Vitreous Hemorrhage obscures view to rule out TRD.
Step 6: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) — Assess for Macular Edema or VMT.

sections.title: 8. Medical Management Protocols
content: Corticosteroids: Mainstay for active perivasculitis (Oral Prednisolone 1mg/kg tapered).
Periocular Injections: Sub-Tenon's Triamcinolone for localized inflammation or CME.
Anti-TB Therapy (ATT): Considered if Mantoux is strongly positive (though controversial).
Anti-VEGF: Intravitreal Ranibizumab or Bevacizumab for NVE regression or pre-op.
Antioxidants: Vitamin C and E supplements often used based on oxidative stress theory.

sections.title: 9. Laser & Surgical Intervention
content: Step 1: Sectoral PRP — Target areas of non-perfusion identified on FFA.
Step 2: 360-degree Peripheral Laser — If widespread ischemia is present.
Step 3: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) — Indicated for non-clearing VH (>1-3 months).
Step 4: Membrane Peeling — For TRD or epiretinal membranes.
Step 5: Endolaser — During PPV to ensure all ischemic areas are treated.

sections.title: 10. Red Flags: Emergency Signs
content: Sudden 'Shower of floaters' or 'black curtain' (Vitreous Hemorrhage).
Fixed shadow in vision (Tractional Retinal Detachment).
Severe eye pain and redness (Neovascular Glaucoma).
Rapid vision loss in a previously 'quiet' eye.
Strongly positive Mantoux (>20mm) or abnormal CXR (suggests active TB).

content.explanation: E: Early adulthood (Young males); A: Areas of non-perfusion (Peripheral); L: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis/Inflammation; E: Exclude other causes; S: Sea-fan neovascularization.

sections.title: 12. Key Clinical Pearls
content: The hallmark of Eales is peripheral venous sheathing; arterial involvement is rare.
Always check the 'good' eye; Eales is often bilateral but asymmetric.
Ultra-widefield FFA is the gold standard for management decisions.
Wait at least 48 hours after Anti-VEGF before Vitrectomy to reduce 'crunch' syndrome (though less common in Eales than DM).

sections.title: 13. Complications & Prognosis
sections.content: Visual prognosis is generally good if treated before Stage IIIb. Complications include recurrent Vitreous Hemorrhage, Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD), Macular ERM, and Neovascular Glaucoma (NVG). Chronic macular edema is the leading cause of persistent visual morbidity.

sections.title: 14. Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
content: PCR for M. Tuberculosis: Nested PCR on aqueous/vitreous samples shows TB DNA in many Eales patients.
Proteomics: Identification of unique inflammatory markers (IL-6, MCP-1) in vitreous.
UWF-Imaging: Ultra-widefield fundus photography has revolutionized staging and laser targeting.
